baseline.purpose: Characterize externally observable behavior before simplification. This is an inventory and characterization baseline, not a normalized old/new differential harness.

preserve: public routes, redirects, rendered metadata, and static-export crawlability
public and site-data API method, authentication, header, cache, body, and error behavior
publication atomicity, freshness, generation, and recoverable job outcomes
Telegram ingress, authorization, mutation, delivery, and outbound-message effects
site/ops security gates and operational status behavior
outOfScopeUntilW3: normalized API differential drivers and golden comparators
reusable provider, status, D1, and Telegram scenario factories
hydration, nonblank, accessibility, SEO, and visual old/new route-class comparison
scope.w3Assignment: W3 owns reusable scenario builders and normalized differential/golden comparison. Existing focused tests are characterization evidence only; this corpus does not claim they provide complete differential coverage.

contracts.preserves: Representative static-export route rendering, light-theme layout, responsive viewport behavior, and absence of document-level horizontal overflow.

snapshotPolicy.capture: viewport only; each class is captured once at each representative viewport
fixtures: Telegram public pulse endpoint is fulfilled with a fixed payload.
Telegram Mini App SDK and session endpoint are fulfilled with fixed signed-launch fixtures.

contracts.preserves: Canonical metadata, robots directives, sitemap/static route output, structured data, OG route availability, and crawlable static-export HTML.
representativeScenarios: Home, discovery, analytics, detail, Telegram public, and Mini App route metadata remain route-appropriate.
Static export remains servable with document cache/CSP rules and Mini App noindex behavior.
Anonymous health/OG/API-access smoke remains available as recorded in W0 evidence.

contracts.preserves: Endpoint paths and methods, public-versus-admin access, site-data eligibility, cache-bypass policy, required headers, response-body shape, pagination, and error semantics.
representativeScenarios: Public GET endpoints retain declared route mapping, cache policy, public API key gate, site-data lane eligibility, body shape, and pagination behavior.
Protected endpoints reject missing or invalid credentials and admin mutations retain their required access checks.
Unknown paths, unsupported methods, and upstream/cache failures retain status/header/error behavior.
Health, report-card, peg-summary, stability-index, liquidity, yield, stress, mint/burn, reserves, depeg-event, and event public projections retain their established contracts.
contracts.w3Required: Normalize request inputs and compare status, selected headers, cache directives, body, and error envelopes across old/new implementations.

contracts.preserves: Scheduled slot selection, provider/dependency budget behavior, published generation atomicity, cache/D1 projection consistency, freshness sentinels, and recoverable degraded outcomes.
representativeScenarios: Scheduled dispatcher runs only the correct cron lane and records skip/degradation semantics.
Report-card publication rejects a shrunken active set before publishing projections.
Yield publication stages and atomically finalizes generation/cache/current/history outputs, preserving the previous published state on validation or finalization failure.
Freshness state and publication cache behavior remain coherent across normal, paused, and degraded runs.
contracts.w3Required: Create output/checksum and freshness comparisons with provider and storage fault injection; do not use private SQL text as the contract.

contracts.preserves: Webhook secret verification, anti-abuse/rate limits, private/group authorization, command and callback effects, Mini App signed-session behavior, idempotent mutation fences, pending queue lifecycle, delivery routing, and user-visible replies.
representativeScenarios: Current and previous webhook secrets authenticate; absent or invalid secrets are rejected and observed without leaking authorization.
Commands/callbacks reject unauthorized group mutations before writes, retain confirmation and idempotency fences, and return user-facing acknowledgements.
Signed Mini App session/mutation flows enforce freshness, portability, and rate limits while preview/unsupported hosts receive no sensitive session.
Queued alerts retain routing, snooze, preference, retry/backoff, effect-fence, and transport-outage behavior.
contracts.w3Required: Build reusable Telegram input/state factories and send-disabled transcript/payload comparisons before refactoring delivery internals.

contracts.preserves: Public API key and admin authorization boundaries, Pages site-data origin/referrer gate, CSP parity, ops asset/host gates, scheduled health/status observability, and cache/header security behavior.
representativeScenarios: Anonymous public access remains limited to declared exemptions; invalid or absent API/admin credentials fail closed.
Only allowed browser origins/referrers reach same-origin site-data proxies.
Static export emits the documented CSP and Mini App robots restrictions.
Ops routes retain host, asset, and authorization gates; status keeps scheduled and data-quality projections.
